L9: # Title:BANGLAPLAN: A Benchmark for Constraint-Based Planning and Decision-Making in Bangla
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite5†Md Rayhanul Masud , cite6†S M Maksudul Alam , cite7†Mohammad Jaminur Islam L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled BANGLAPLAN: A Benchmark for Constraint-Based Planning and Decision-Making in Bangla, by Md Rayhanul Masud and 2 other authors
L14: 
L15: cite8†View PDF cite9†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) increasingly help users arrange appointments, plan journeys, and allocate limited resources. These tasks require models to satisfy constraints on time, cost, capacity, and order, or determine that no feasible solution exists. Bangla is the world's seventh most widely spoken language, and existing benchmarks cover many language and reasoning tasks. However, benchmarks for evaluating planning and decision-making in Bangla under explicit constraints remain lacking.
L17: We introduce BANGLAPLAN, a benchmark of 1,000 problems across ten task families grounded in everyday life and institutions in Bangladesh. It includes feasible and infeasible problems in four language registers: everyday, formal, colloquial, and Bangla--English mixed. Answers cover eight structured types, including schedules, routes, allocations, and ordered steps, in a common JSON format. We construct the benchmark through language-model-assisted drafting and independent human validation.
L18: We evaluate 11 open-weight and proprietary model configurations using exact match, separately reporting feasible-case accuracy, infeasibility detection, and format errors. We find a large performance gap: GPT-6.1 Sol achieves 98.7% accuracy and Qwen3.5-27B with thinking reaches 80.3%, while direct-answer configurations score at most 30.9%. Seven of eleven configurations perform below the always-``infeasible'' baseline.
L19: Our findings also suggest that harder problems primarily reduce plan-construction accuracy, while infeasibility detection remains more robust. BANGLAPLAN provides a reproducible basis for evaluating planning and decision-making in Bangla. BANGLAPLAN is available at: cite10†this https URL†github.com .

L9: # Title:Designing Textual Interfaces To Enhance Llm Reasoning On Audio-Visual Question Answering
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite5†Yi Wang , cite6†Tianzi Wang , cite7†Tong Lei , cite8†Dahan Wang , cite9†Peter Bell L12:

L14: 
L15: cite10†View PDF cite11†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:Automatic prompt optimization (APO) has shown strong effectiveness for text-based LLMs and LLM systems, but its application to audio-visual understanding systems requires suitable textual interfaces through which multimodal reasoning can be exposed to text-based optimizers. We investigate how the design of textual interfaces affects prompt optimization for multimodal reasoning, on the audio-visual question answering task.
L17: We compare three interface designs, including a direct inference system consisting of a single omni-modal large language model (OmniLLM), a captioner-reasoner system, and an agentic architecture in which a primary agent orchestrates subagent OmniLLMs.
L18: Experiments with Qwen3-Omni and Gemini show that direct prompt optimization provides model-dependent gains; the captioner-reasoner system and the agentic system expose more interpretable optimization interfaces but are harder to optimize, where error analysis of cases affected by optimization is conducted. Our study highlights textual interface design as an important factor in making prompt optimization effective for omni-modal reasoning systems. Our implementation details are specified in GitHub repo.
